preconditions.description: The input integers n and m satisfy 1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 100,000 and the difference n - m is at most 2,000.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == m and all(c in '()' for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s has length exactly m and consists only of the characters '(' and ')'.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the number of valid (p, q) pairs modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout) == sum(1 for p in generate_valid_p(s) for q in generate_valid_q(s, p) if is_valid(p + s + q)) % (10**9 + 7)
postconditions.description: The output equals the count of all pairs (p, q) such that p + s + q is a valid sequence of round brackets, computed modulo 10^9 + 7. A valid sequence must have equal numbers of '(' and ')', and for every prefix, the number of '(' is at least the number of ')'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(p) + len(s) + len(q) == n for p in generate_valid_p(s) for q in generate_valid_q(s, p) if is_valid(p + s + q))
postconditions.description: Every valid pair (p, q) satisfies that the total length of p + s + q equals n.
